name: ukiyo-e
style: a Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print in the manner of Hokusai and Hiroshige: flat areas of colour inside fine black key-block outlines, Prussian blue and indigo, ochre and sage-green grounds, vermilion accents, cream paper showing through, subtle woodgrain and soft bokashi gradients, stylised curling waves and patterned foliage; flat, clear and decorative, never photographic or 3D-rendered

rules.backdrop: A woodblock landscape print: a bird's-eye view or a high horizon, the sky in bands of bokashi colour, stylised waves and clouds, a few small figures at most. Flat colour, no photographic depth.
rules.scene: A woodblock print scene: one to three figures doing one clear action, strong outlines, flat colour, patterned clothing, a simple setting. Every era keeps the print language: machines, ships and cities of later ages are drawn as woodblock prints too.
rules.bust: A woodblock portrait: one person's head and shoulders, strong outline, flat colour, patterned clothing, a plain cream ground.
rules.figure: A full-length woodblock figure like a game token: strong outline, flat colour, patterned clothing, a clear silhouette with a thin cream outline around it.
rules.object: A woodblock-print building or object seen from a high three-quarter angle like a game token: crisp black outlines, flat colour in terracotta, indigo and ochre, a thin cream outline around the silhouette, no ground under it.

map_rules: The map is one continuous painted ground seen straight down; the grid is never drawn.
Units are flat print tokens with a thin cream outline; a stack shows a numbered count seal, not more figures.
Cities are clearly bigger than units.
Farms, paddies and mines are painted into the ground; railroads are thin.
All factions and eras share the same ground language; only costume and architecture change.
